title: Alert Curve Stabilizer + Autoresolve Runbook Compiler for Multi‑Region Failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: reduce noisy pages during transients and planned multi-region failovers while preserving high-fidelity SLO breach signals. Deliver an 'Alert Curve Stabilizer' that adaptively smooths short-lived spikes (temporal suppression + exponential backoff) and a Runbook Compiler that turns telemetry-triggered templates into executable, auditable playbooks. The stabilizer will operate at the alerting layer (pre-pager) and use signal-sidecar scoring (rate, error-budget burn rate, region affinity, customer tier) to decide temporary suppression vs immediate escalation. The Runbook Compiler will synthesize a minimal automated remediation (e.g., circuit trip, throttling config change, deploy fallback model variant) and attach clear human steps if escalation occurs. We will ensure graceful load shedding rules are applied before global cutovers, with canary windows on traffic-steering and explicit SLO guardrails to avoid cascading failures.
acceptance_criteria: False-positive paging rate for regional transient incidents reduced by >=70% on staging traces
SLO-relevant alerts remain >=95% recall for simulated degradations (no >5% loss of true SLO breaches)
Automated runbook actions have a reversible execution path and an audit entry in the incident log
Multi-region failover drill completes with <3% customer-facing error-rate delta and no manual escalation required for control-plane failures
Circuit breaker thresholds and load-shedding policies can be tuned via Console feature flags and rolled back during rollout
